title: Gurman: Siri Layoffs Spared Newer AI Systems, But Problems Persist
excerpt: Apple's recent Siri layoffs affected employees working on the assistant's older infrastructure rather than its newer AI systems, according to...
content_html:
Apple's recent Siri layoffs affected employees working on the assistant's older infrastructure rather than its newer AI systems, according to Bloomberg's Mark Gurman.


In his latest "Power On" newsletter, Gurman said employees have yet to notice a major difference in how Apple operates despite efforts to accelerate development and spread significant releases throughout the year. He added that the company faces growing competition from AI developers that update their models and services far more frequently than Apple's annual operating system cycle.

Within software engineering chief Craig Federighi's organization, Apple apparently follows an internal release calendar labeled A through G, with engineering work tied to specific software versions and launch windows. Depending on the release, the roadmap and features for a major operating system update are largely determined by late summer or early fall of the preceding year.

Gurman argued that this structure leaves Apple with limited flexibility to respond to competitors' breakthroughs during the subsequent development cycle. Gurman also criticized ‌Siri‌'s slow responses, limited third-party integration, and seemingly worsening dictation.

Apple is reportedly developing a more advanced AI agent, but Gurman does not expect it to arrive before late 2027. He warned that rival agents could become difficult to abandon as they accumulate users' preferences and connected accounts, although Apple's reputation for privacy and deeper platform access could help it compete. ‌Siri‌'s multistep control of Apple apps is expected to launch in December, with third-party app support following in 2027.
